---
title: Pages for agents
description: A Markdown copy of each page, and an index of them, for language models and coding agents.
order: 6
---

A language model reads Markdown more easily than a web page. The navbar, the sidebar and the scripts of a
page are noise to it. So smalldocs can write a Markdown copy of each page, and an index of the copies, the
file `llms.txt`. A coding agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, can then read the site's documentation as
plain text.

smalldocs does this as Quarto does it, with the same option and the same file names. Quarto added the
option in version 1.9.

## Turn it on

Set `llms-txt: true` under `website`. The key is the same in `_smalldocs.yml` and in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
website:
  title: My project
  description: What my project does
  llms-txt: true
```

The option is off unless you set it. A site without it builds as before, and the option changes no HTML
page.

## What a build writes

With the option on, a build writes two more kinds of file into the output folder:

- **A Markdown copy of each page.** It goes beside the page, with `.llms.md` in place of `.html`. So
  `guide/config.html` gets `guide/config.llms.md`.
- **`llms.txt`**, at the top of the site. It has the title of the site, its description, and a list of
  the pages, each with a link to its copy. With `site-url` set, the links are full addresses.

This site turns the option on. Here are its files:

- The index: [llms.txt](/llms.txt).
- This page, [llms.qmd](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs/blob/main/docs/guide/llms.qmd), and its
  copy, [llms.llms.md](llms.llms.md).
- The page on writing,
  [markdown.qmd](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs/blob/main/docs/guide/markdown.qmd), and its copy,
  [markdown.llms.md](markdown.llms.md). It shows callouts, tabs, tables, maths and footnotes.
- A notebook,
  [notebooks.ipynb](https://github.com/rahuldave/smalldocs/blob/main/docs/guide/notebooks.ipynb), and its
  copy, [notebooks.llms.md](notebooks.llms.md). The copy holds the code and the saved outputs.

## What a copy holds

A copy is made from the built page. So it holds what the reader sees, after includes, shortcodes and
notebook outputs. It is GitHub-flavoured Markdown, the Markdown of GitHub's own pages.

- The title of the page, its subtitle and its description come first.
- The navbar, the sidebar, the breadcrumbs, the table of contents and the footer are left out.
- A link to another page of the site goes to that page's copy. A link to another site stays as it is.
- A callout is a quote. Its first line is its kind, such as `**NOTE:**` or `**TIP:**`.
- Each tab of a tabset becomes a heading, followed by the tab's content.
- Code keeps its language. A notebook's printed output is a code block with no language.
- Maths is between dollars, `$...$` and `$$...$$`.
- A table's caption follows the table.
- Footnotes go to the end of the copy, under the heading Footnotes.
- A picture is a Markdown image. A picture held inside the page, such as a notebook's plot, is not a file.
  So the copy names it, as `[Image: its caption]`.

## Content for agents only

The format `llms-txt` lets a block be only in the copy, or only on the page:

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="llms-txt"}
Only the Markdown copy has this paragraph.
:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="llms-txt"}
Only the HTML page has this paragraph.
:::
```

In the copy, a condition on `llms-txt` decides alone. On the HTML page, `llms-txt` is a format that does
not hold, as `pdf` does not.

## Drafts and the 404 page

A draft that a build leaves out has no copy. A draft with `draft-mode: unlinked` is built, but it has no
copy and no line in `llms.txt`. The 404 page has a copy, but no line in `llms.txt`, as in Quarto.

## The copies are not pages

The copies are written only into the output folder. smalldocs never reads the output folder as pages,
and `smalldocs preview` does not watch it. So the next build does not read a copy as a page.

A page may link to `llms.txt` or to a copy, as this page does. smalldocs keeps such a link as it is, and
does not report it as broken.

## How it differs from Quarto

Quarto turns each built page into Markdown with Pandoc. smalldocs has no Pandoc, so it does the same in
Python. The copies follow Quarto's rules, but a few details differ:

- A definition list is each term in bold, followed by its definition.
- A task list keeps its boxes, `[x]` and `[ ]`.
- A figure's caption is the alt text of its picture.
- A subscript or a superscript is plain text, so H~2~O is H2O.
- A picture held inside the page is named, not copied into the Markdown.
- A dollar sign in the text is written `\$`, so that it is not read as maths.
